article.title: Nvidia Bears Add to Wagers as Competition Threatens Its Dominance: Short Seller Tracker
article.text:
Meta Says AI Compute Isn’t Enough: Is the Infrastructure Selloff Over?
5.3M Views · 140 Posts
$NVIDIA (NVDA.US)$ faced mounting pressure after bears added to their wagers against the chip giant amid increasing competition that threatened to challenge its dominance in the market for semiconductors that power artificial intelligence workloads.
Trading in borrowed Nvidia shares that were sold short rose to 13.61 million shares Wednesday, from 11.69 million shares a day earlier, exchange data tracked by moomoo showed. The latest figure represented 9.2% of the shares that changed hands yesterday, when the stock advanced 3.7%, the biggest gain in five weeks. Shorting involves shares sold without the seller owning them, which is a common practice used to profit from a potential decline in a stock's price.
$Meta Platforms (META.US)$ is reportedly planning to start manufacturing its AI chip in September, Reuters reported Thursday, citing the company’s internal memo. The social media giant that’s looking to compete with $Amazon (AMZN.US)$ , $Microsoft (MSFT.US)$ and $Alphabet-A (GOOGL.US)$ in providing AI cloud services, is working with $Broadcom (AVGO.US)$ to design and $Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US)$ to manufacture the AI chips, according to the report.
Meta is Nvidia’s fifth largest customer, behind Microsoft, Amazon, $Super Micro Computer (SMCI.US)$ and Alphabet, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.
Still, sales of Nvidia’s Taiwanese assembly partners climbed in June, signaling continued strong demand. Quanta, which supplies AI servers powered by Nvidia’s GPUs, saw its monthly sales more than double to 385.19 billion New Taiwanese dollars in June from a year earlier, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.
$HON HAI PRECISION INDUSTRY SPON GDS EACH REP 2 SHS TWD10 REG'S' (HNHPF.US)$ , Nvidia’s server assembly partner, saw a 52% surge in monthly sales in June to NT$ 821.8 billion, allowing the Taiwanese company to post a bigger-than-expected 40% surge in quarterly sales, according to Bloomberg.
NVIDIA recently issued a statement to Bloomberg denying claims of a technical delay, confirming that its product roadmap remains intact. This clarification serves as a counterweight to concerns that infrastructure bottlenecks could disrupt the company’s competitive lead in the artificial intelligence sector.
The stock is also navigating a complex geopolitical environment as China moves to grant limited approval for domestic firms to purchase H200 processors. While this policy shift eases access to Nvidia’s technology, companies must now request individual approval for specific quantities and use cases.
Regulators are simultaneously intensifying their oversight, with the French competition authority announcing Thursday that its antitrust investigation into the company is nearing a conclusion. This probe focuses on allegations of anti-competitive practices within the cloud-AI and GPU markets.

thesis.description: How far will the US crackdown on advanced AI-chip exports to third countries escalate — will the US Commerce Department go beyond its May 2026 guidance and impose formal licensing requirements or other escalated restrictions on AI-chip shipments to third countries such as Malaysia, Singapore and Japan by Nvidia's FY2027 year-end?
thesis.outcome: Whether the US Commerce Department / Bureau of Industry and Security moves beyond its May 2026 guidance to a binding export-licensing rule or other escalated restriction on AI-chip shipments to third countries, and the resulting constraint on Nvidia's sales to those markets.
thesis.period: Nvidia's FY2027 year-end (late January 2027) — set by the reason: a pending regulatory decision is tracked to the current fiscal year-end.
thesis.settled_by: A US Commerce Department / Bureau of Industry and Security Federal Register rule, licence requirement or formal export-control action.
thesis.why_a_separate_bet: clean-5 turns on Beijing's decision whether to allow Chinese commercial buyers to purchase H200 chips the US cleared in December 2025; this thesis turns on Washington's decision whether to tighten third-country diversion controls. The two can move independently — Beijing could reopen H200 purchases while Washington hardens third-country rules, or Washington could act while Beijing stays closed.

article.title: Nvidia halves Asia buyer list in China chip crackdown, steps up due diligence: report
article.text:
NVIDIA has more than halved the number of Asian customers authorised to buy its AI chips after creating a new “white list” of companies that have passed tougher compliance checks aimed at preventing the products from reaching China, the Financial Times reported on Monday (Jul 14).
Over the past few months, the chipmaker has intensified due diligence in Singapore, Malaysia and Japan, the report added, citing three people familiar with the matter.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours.
The tighter scrutiny comes as the Trump administration seeks to prevent advanced US chips from reaching Chinese entities through third countries.
The US Commerce Department issued guidance in May aimed at curbing advanced AI chips from reaching overseas subsidiaries of Chinese companies, highlighting concerns that Nvidia’s cutting-edge Blackwell processors may have been exported to Chinese-linked entities in countries such as Malaysia despite US restrictions.
Nvidia has tightened compliance procedures following pressure from Washington, the FT said, adding that staff now visit customers’ data centres, verify contracts and interview end users as part of the checks.
The US Department of Commerce is also involved, providing oversight and political backing, the report said.
The department did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. REUTERS
